definitions: A timber and masonry tower crowned with four broad sails, built to convert wind into grinding power on a scale that dwarfs the miller inside it.
colloq. Best described as a barn that got tired of staying put and grew arms instead.
example: Tourists posed beside the thiccc windmill for scale, and the windmill won.
etymology: From wind (Old English 'wind') plus mill (Old English 'myln,' from Latin 'molina,' a grinding place). Dutch windmills reached their broadest proportions in the 18th century, when polder drainage demanded serious girth.
caption: Plate N., A Dutch windmill of substantial cross-section, out-massing the canal beside it.
